verdict: Fortinet's revenue rose 20% to $2.08B as product sales jumped 37%, billings grew 29%, and profit rose 34% to $636M.

segments.name: Service
segments.note: Subscriptions and support — security services and FortiGuard threat intelligence attached to the installed base; the recurring majority of revenue.

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Firewalls and other security appliances — up 37% as customers refreshed hardware for AI-era traffic.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: The sales force and marketing behind Fortinet's security products.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Engineering the FortiGate platform, FortiOS and the wider security fabric.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: G&A of $59.6M, partly offset by a $1.4M gain on intellectual-property matters — shown net so the chart foots to reported operating income.

otherDetail: Interest income of $42.7M on Fortinet's cash pile, plus $11.0M of other income, less $3.0M of interest expense.

takeaways.title: Hardware came roaring back
takeaways.text: Product revenue grew 37% to $765M — a strong appliance refresh cycle — while the larger service business grew 13% to $1.31B on subscriptions and support.

takeaways.title: Billings point to more growth
takeaways.text: Billings of $2.34B grew 29%, faster than revenue, and management raised full-year billings guidance for the third time this year — deferred revenue built up for future quarters.

takeaways.title: Profitability stayed elite
takeaways.text: GAAP operating margin was 34% (38% non-GAAP) and operating cash flow was $946M — Fortinet converts an unusual share of sales into cash for a company growing this fast.
